checkOutcomes.evidence: Trace measured LCP/FCP 2.80s; mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 6.3s and Speed Index 7.9s.
Mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.043 and Lighthouse measured 0.022, both within the good range.
Trace recorded two long tasks, longest 144.65ms, and 166.54ms total blocking time on the desktop load.
HAR recorded 40 requests and 2,051,856 transferred bytes for the login/consent surface.
HAR recorded 24 scripts transferring 1,325,452 bytes for a small unauthenticated login/consent surface.
Lighthouse accessibility found missing labels and required ARIA attributes; the image audit found four cookie-card images without alt text.
Lighthouse color-contrast audit failed on the mobile login route.
No h1 was present, and the focus probe found no visible outline or box shadow on focused login controls and links.
Desktop screenshot showed readable body text with comfortable line lengths inside the consent dialog.
No viewport meta was present on desktop; mobile Lighthouse also failed its viewport scaling audit.
Lighthouse reported browser console errors.
Doctype and UTF-8 were valid, but all four images lacked a complete width/height pair and used PNG without responsive sources.
Lighthouse reported a deprecated API, missing source maps, four BFCache failure reasons, and console errors.
The title is only “Facebook”; no meta description was present.
Links had real hrefs, but the page omitted the viewport meta and robots.txt disallowed User-agent: *.
The response succeeded and exposed a canonical, but robots.txt disallowed all generic crawlers and /sitemap.xml returned an HTML unavailable state.
The probe found no Open Graph metadata and no description on the entry page.
HTTPS, CSP, HSTS, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, and Permissions-Policy were present; no cookies or exposed secrets were observed before consent.
Before consent, cookies reported zero cookies and trackers reported no known tracker domains; only Meta-controlled delivery origins were observed.
No permission prompt appeared on load, and the username input advertised autocomplete="username webauthn".
Headers probe found no Referrer-Policy and CSP style-src included unsafe-inline.
Discoverability measured only 1% raw-to-rendered content coverage and classified the page as a JS shell.

paths.description: Public entry/login and consent surface, representing the unauthenticated homepage and primary entry task.
Registration route, representing account creation; cookie modal inspected, completion not attempted because it creates an account.
Password recovery route, representing account recovery; cookie modal inspected, identity-dependent continuation not attempted.
Feed, profile, messaging, media, settings, commerce, and long-lived authenticated journeys were not covered because no test account was provided.

findings.summary: The public entry surface does not honor dark color preference.
findings.evidence: Dark-emulation screenshot remained a hard-coded white dialog and grey backdrop; computed color-scheme was normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and theme surfaces with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: A first-load cookie wall obscures every tested primary route, especially on mobile.
findings.evidence: Desktop, registration, recovery, and mobile screenshots all opened with a modal cookie wall covering the primary content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact consent surface that preserves access to the primary task, keeps equal consent choices, and avoids loading explanatory cards into the initial modal.

findings.summary: The mobile experience is a scaled 980px desktop layout and zoom/reflow support is compromised.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout reported no viewport meta and rendered a 980 CSS-pixel layout scaled to 360 physical pixels; text and controls are miniaturised.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a standard device-width viewport, preserve user scaling, and reflow the login and consent UI at narrow widths.

findings.summary: The entry surface paints too slowly and performs avoidable main-thread work.
findings.evidence: Trace measured LCP/FCP 2.80s; mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 6.3s and Speed Index 7.9s.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce critical JS, prioritize the LCP content, and split/defer long tasks so the login task paints within the good LCP range.

findings.summary: The unauthenticated login/consent surface ships 2.05MB, dominated by 1.33MB across 24 scripts.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 24 scripts transferring 1,325,452 bytes for a small unauthenticated login/consent surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a minimal unauthenticated bundle; defer consent-detail and authenticated-product code until requested.

findings.summary: Accessibility checks found contrast, labelling, ARIA, heading, focus visibility, and target-size gaps.
findings.evidence: No h1 was present, and the focus probe found no visible outline or box shadow on focused login controls and links.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic headings and controls, preserve visible :focus-visible styles, fix labels/ARIA, add meaningful alt text, and verify contrast.

findings.summary: The entry page has generic and incomplete search/share metadata.
findings.evidence: The title is only “Facebook”; no meta description was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a descriptive title, meta description, and accurate Open Graph metadata for the public entry page.

findings.summary: Non-JavaScript clients receive almost none of the visible login content.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 1% raw-to-rendered content coverage and classified the page as a JS shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the essential login purpose, fields, recovery/signup links, and consent choices so the core entry task survives without JavaScript.

findings.evidence: Headers probe found no Referrer-Policy and CSP style-src included unsafe-inline.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an explicit strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter Referrer-Policy and continue reducing unsafe-inline style dependencies with hashes/nonces.

findings.summary: Cookie-dialog images lack dimensions, alternatives, responsive sources, lazy loading, and modern formats.
findings.evidence: Doctype and UTF-8 were valid, but all four images lacked a complete width/height pair and used PNG without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width and height, appropriate alt or empty alt, lazy loading below fold, srcset/sizes, and AVIF/WebP variants.

findings.summary: Lighthouse found console errors, deprecated API use, missing source maps, and BFCache blockers.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported a deprecated API, missing source maps, four BFCache failure reasons, and console errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove console/runtime errors and deprecated APIs, ship valid source maps, and resolve BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: The retained heap footprint is large for the visible public task.
findings.evidence: A static login/consent page retained about 43.8MB self size across roughly 860k to 877k heap nodes, disproportionate to the visible task.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile dominators and remove unauthenticated code/data not needed by login or consent; remeasure in one controlled session.

findings.summary: The password field omits the current-password autocomplete token.
findings.evidence: Username used username webauthn, but the password field had an empty autocomplete token rather than current-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete="current-password" on the password field while retaining username webauthn on the identifier field.
